title: Fourier concentration and spectral sampling
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$, and let $\mathcal F$ be any family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The sum of the squared Fourier coefficients of $f$ over sets outside $\mathcal F$ is at most $\varepsilon$ if and only if a random set sampled with probability proportional to the squared Fourier coefficients of $f$ lies outside $\mathcal F$ with probability at most $\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathcal F$ is a family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$
